title: Utah Residents Protest Data Centers at Planning Commission Meeting

tea.why: Residents opposed a proposed ordinance allowing new data center construction in mining, grazing, and industrial zones.
tea.want: They demanded the rejection of data center construction rules and accountability for police actions.
tea.changed: Oct 24: Public backlash and online criticism intensified following the circulation of a video showing a deputy body-slamming a protester.

summary: Scores of residents turned out at a Utah County Planning Commission meeting in Provo, Utah, to protest against proposed regulations allowing new data center construction. According to reports, commissioners only allowed members of the public to speak after voting to approve the ordinance. The demonstration led to tensions and the physical restraint and arrest of participants by sheriff's deputies. A video of an officer throwing a participant face-first to the floor drew widespread online criticism and public backlash, with the affected activist calling for the deputy's dismissal.
demands: Reject proposed data center construction regulations
Fire the deputy involved in the physical restraint
response: Sheriff's deputies restrained and arrested participants during the meeting. According to Democracy Now!, an activist was charged with disrupting a meeting and assaulting a police officer. The sheriff's office alleged the activist kicked an officer, an allegation the activist denied.

injuries.text: concussion and bruises to her jaw, shoulder and knee

updates.text: Scores of residents protested data center regulations at a Utah County Planning Commission meeting in Provo.
Reports highlighted that sheriff's deputies violently restrained three people, resulting in charges and injuries.
Public backlash grew online after a video of a deputy body-slamming a protester amassed over a million views.
